draft.title: Volume of pyramids and cones
card: A pyramid has one third of the volume of the prism with the same base and the same height. A cone has one third of the volume of the cylinder with the same base and height.
For both solids, \(V = \frac{1}{3}Ah\). Here \(A\) is the area of the base and \(h\) is the perpendicular height, the straight-up height from the base to the tip.
For a cone, the base is a circle, so \(A = \pi r^{2}\) and \(V = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^{2}h\). Do not use the slant height for \(h\).
A square pyramid has a base of side 6 cm and a height of 10 cm. \(A = 6 \times 6 = 36\), so \(V = \frac{1}{3} \times 36 \times 10 = 120\text{ cm}^{3}\).
draft.remember: Find the base area, multiply by the perpendicular height, then divide by 3.

a.q: A cone has radius 3 cm and perpendicular height 4 cm. What is its volume, in terms of \(\pi\)?
a.why: \(V = \frac{1}{3} \times \pi \times 3^{2} \times 4 = \frac{1}{3} \times 36\pi = 12\pi\). The option \(36\pi\text{ cm}^{3}\) is the volume of the cylinder, because it skips the division by 3.
a.clue: Find the base area first, then take one third.

b.q: A square pyramid has a base of side 8 cm and a slant height of 5 cm on each triangular face. Its perpendicular height is 3 cm. What is its volume?
b.why: Use the perpendicular height: \(V = \frac{1}{3} \times 64 \times 3 = 64\text{ cm}^{3}\). Using the slant height 5 instead gives \(\frac{1}{3} \times 64 \times 5 = \frac{320}{3}\), which is the tempting mix-up. The option \(192\text{ cm}^{3}\) skips the division by 3.
b.clue: Which of the two heights goes straight up from the base?

wants.brief: A square pyramid and a cone side by side. On each, a dashed vertical line from the tip to the centre of the base is labelled perpendicular height h. A sloping edge from the tip to the base edge is labelled slant height. The base of each is labelled base area A.
wants.why: It shows which height to use in the formula and which one to ignore.
